This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #25884: OpenAI server_is_overloaded stream errors are not retried (same core symptom — overloaded stream errors not entering retry flow)
- #25730: Codex server_is_overloaded stream errors are not retried (same nested error shape and retry classification gap)

The analysis in this issue is detailed and appreciated — if you believe the wrapped `Error(JSON.stringify(...))` path represents a distinct unaddressed gap not covered by those issues, please add a comment clarifying that distinction so maintainers can triage accordingly.

Thanks for the duplicate check.

I agree this is related to #25884 / #25730 / #25886 / #25728, but I believe this issue tracks one additional path that those fixes do not cover.

The existing fixes handle the stream payload when it reaches `ProviderError.parseStreamError()`, for example as `{ message: JSON.stringify(payload) }`.

The gap here is specifically when the same stream payload is wrapped as an actual `Error` instance:

```ts
new Error(JSON.stringify({
  type: "error",
  error: {
    type: "service_unavailable_error",
    code: "server_is_overloaded",
  },
}))
```

In the current `MessageV2.fromError()` flow, this hits the `e instanceof Error` branch before the `default` branch can call `ProviderError.parseStreamError()`:

```ts
case e instanceof Error:
  return new NamedError.Unknown({ message: errorMessage(e) }, { cause: e }).toObject()

default:
  const parsed = ProviderError.parseStreamError(e)
```

So even after #25888 / #25886-style fixes, this wrapped `Error(JSON.stringify(...))` path can still become `UnknownError` and bypass retry.

I think the remaining fix is to attempt `ProviderError.parseStreamError(e)` before converting generic `Error` instances to `UnknownError`, plus a regression test for the wrapped `Error(JSON.stringify(...))` case.

Confirming this with a local LM Studio setup:

- **Provider:** `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` → LM Studio on macOS (M1 Max 64GB)
- **Model:** Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni 30B A3B (Q4_K_M GGUF) — multimodal (vision + audio + text)
- **LM Studio reports:** `vision: true`, `trainedForToolUse: true`

Same behavior: clipboard image pasted in OpenCode TUI, model responds "I'm unable to process images directly" — but the exact same model works perfectly when sending `image_url` content parts via direct curl to the same LM Studio endpoint.

Interestingly, **pi** (another agent framework using the same `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` transport) handles this correctly with a simple `"vision": true` flag in its model config. Pi passes images through to the model and they work.

Adding weight to the hypothesis that the `file → image_url` translation is missing for custom OpenAI-compatible providers. A config-level `supports_attachments: true` on the model entry would solve this for all local/custom multimodal models.

Again, I think we're seeing several opportunities to make opencode better.  Issue counts have grown from around 4,400 to over 4,700 in the couple of months that I've been reporting OC issues.  Ensuring OC is really great at creating issues with all the details you need for debugging would be more important than fixing this issue or the 6-8 I have opened that haven't had any progress in getting fixed, at least from what I'm seeing in my tickets.  Also, tickets it did help me open usually failed because they didn't meet OC's own ticket requirements, often failing for being too much AI generated content.  Someone may have spent more time locking down ticket requirements instead of making OC great at helping agents report all of the accurate/clear details needed.  OC is an AI tool, it doesn't seem to make a lot of sense to be critical of AI generated content in ticket details.  I'd open a new ticket to suggest this as a feature and suggest it gets high priority, but the ticket would probably be flagged as a feature request duplicate or declined because I typed out too many details, or it would be accepted assigned and left for months without any movement.
